sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Storage Create failure path calls `recordLegacyDuration` with the storage start time. WHY: Storage errors pollute legacy latency/error metrics and hide unified-store failures from alerts. HOW: Call `recordStorageDuration` on the storage error branch.

WHAT: Storage Update failure path calls `recordLegacyDuration` with the storage timer. WHY: Same metric misattribution as Create masks unified-store update failures and inflates legacy error rate. HOW: Call `recordStorageDuration` when `d.Storage.Update` fails.

WHAT: Delete success passes `name` where all other calls pass `options.Kind`. WHY: Creates unbounded high-cardinality label values per object name and breaks kind-based dashboards. HOW: Pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`.

WHAT: Async legacy DeleteCollection records via `recordStorageDuration`. WHY: Legacy latency/errors are attributed to unified storage, corrupting both backends SLOs. HOW: Call `recordLegacyDuration` for the legacy branch.

WHAT: Async legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection failures only record a metric and never log the error. WHY: Divergences between unified and legacy stores become invisible, defeating the safe-measure purpose of mode 3. HOW: Log the legacy error inside each async goroutine as the prior sync code did.

issues.descricao: Delete puts the base d.Log instead of the enriched per-call logger into the context, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method fields.
issues.textoGolden: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

comentarios.texto: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` installs the mode-level logger instead of the request-scoped `log` built on line 96 (which carries name, kind and method) — a copy/paste error, as every other method in this file passes the composed `log`. Storage.Delete and the legacy delete goroutine therefore log without the per-request fields this PR is adding (and without the metrics method/kind context).
ctx is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of the enriched `log`. The delete logs then lose the name, kind and method values. Use `log`.
The Delete context uses d.Log rather than the per-call log. This is a logging-context inconsistency (not a data leak); use the per-call logger for consistency.

issues.descricao: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
issues.textoGolden: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

comentarios.texto: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

issues.descricao: Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

comentarios.texto: The Delete success-path metric passes `name` where every other call site in this file (lines 48, 103, 113, 156, 159) passes options.Kind in the kind/name argument slot. The storage-success sample for Delete is thus labelled with the object name instead of the resource kind, breaking label consistency with the other operations and with the error sample emitted at line 103. Use options.Kind here (or insert name consistently everywhere, matching the metric's label semantics).
recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) at line 106 passes the object name in the kind label slot.

recordStorageDuration is called with the object `name` as the `kind` label: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. Every other storage call site passes `options.Kind` (lines 73, 89, 103, 156, 159). This injects a per-object value into the kind label, corrupting the metric and giving it unbounded cardinality (one series per object name), which grows memory on every delete. Should be `options.Kind`.

issues.descricao: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

comentarios.texto: On a Storage.Create failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) — the failing subsystem is Storage, not Legacy, and it passes the storage start time. This records storage failures under the legacy metric, corrupting the dual-writer error dashboards (and contradicts the success path on line 48 which uses recordStorageDuration). Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

On a Storage.Update failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), attributing a storage failure and its storage duration to the legacy metric. This is inconsistent with the success path on line 132 (recordStorageDuration) and with mode1's semantics. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

The async goroutine performing the LEGACY DeleteCollection measures it with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Every other legacy write in this file uses recordLegacyDuration (lines 56, 113, 140); recording it under the storage metric reports legacy latency/errors as storage latency/errors. Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

issues.descricao: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

comentarios.texto: The async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns — which is immediately after Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return — so the goroutine's Legacy.Create can be canceled before completing, silently dropping the legacy write that this mode exists to guarantee. The same applies to the goroutines at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Detach the async context from request cancellation (e.g. derive from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background()) before applying the timeout.

The legacy write in Mode 3 became fire-and-forget, changing the contract callers relied on: previously Create (and, identically, Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) returned only after the LegacyStorage call had been made in-request; now it returns immediately and the write runs in a detached goroutine. Worse, the goroutine builds its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), which the API server cancels as soon as the handler returns/flushes the response — so the legacy write and its 10s timeout will typically be cancelled outright and the legacy store silently stops being updated, which is precisely what the new mode-3 integration cases assume still happens. Any detached work must be given a context not tied to the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a server-lifetime context), and consumers that depended on the synchronous legacy write need to be updated.

The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

issues.descricao: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.

comentarios.texto: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Restore forwarding of the committed result via updateWrapper instead of recomputing the update against legacy state.

issues.descricao: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

comentarios.texto: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

issues.descricao: The List error test case is still named 'not implemented' although List is now implemented and the case checks storage error propagation.

comentarios.texto: The test-case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" still describes the old stub List (which returned nil, nil with a "List not implemented" log). List is now implemented at dualwriter_mode3.go:79 and delegates to Storage.List; the case merely checks that a Storage error is propagated. The name contradicts the code it now exercises — rename it, e.g. "error when listing objects in the unified store fails".

issues.descricao: The Create test case name says 'only in the unified store' although Mode 3 also writes to legacy.

comentarios.texto: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

issues.descricao: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

comentarios.texto: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

issues.descricao: The storage-failure Create test registers its failing expectation via setupLegacyFn and only works because legacy and storage share one mock.

comentarios.texto: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers the failing Create expectation only through setupLegacyFn. It passes only because legacy and storage share one mock, so the storage Create gets that error by accident. Register the expectation in setupStorageFn and use separate mocks for legacy and storage, so the test really covers a storage failure.

issues.descricao: DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and written but their results are discarded before the actual encoding at lines 117-121. WHY: This is dead computation from an apparent copy-paste error; it wastes work and misleads readers about how the DER sequence is produced. HOW: Remove lines 114-115 so only the encoders used in the return statement remain.

WHAT: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and used to encode r and s, but their encoded bytes are discarded. WHY: This is dead computation that wastes allocations and indicates an incomplete refactoring; the actual DER sequence is built later with fresh instances. HOW: Remove the two discarded ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls so only the writeDerSeq call produces the output.

WHAT: readLength returns -1 when it encounters the BER indefinite-length marker 0x80. WHY: DER requires definite lengths, so accepting -1 leads to NegativeArraySizeException in readInteger or an empty sequence in readSequence instead of a clear malformed-input error. HOW: Throw an IOException rejecting indefinite-length encoding.

WHAT: readSequence subtracts each element's full byte length from the declared sequence length without checking the element fits. WHY: A malformed element larger than the remaining sequence length can underflow length and exit the loop silently, returning a sequence with fewer elements than declared and masking the corruption. HOW: Validate that bytes.length <= length before subtracting, and verify length reaches exactly 0 after the loop.

issues.descricao: concatenatedRSToASN1DER encodes r and s into two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances before re-encoding them in the return statement.
issues.textoGolden: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls allocate encoders and encode rBigInteger/sBigInteger, but their results are discarded — the returned DER comes entirely from the expression at lines 117-121, which re-encodes the same BigIntegers. These two statements have no effect and should be removed (they are a leftover from an earlier formulation).

Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` encode values and discard the results. The return expression re-encodes the same values, so these lines are dead computation left over from a copy-paste or refactor. Remove them.

issues.descricao: order() is added to CryptoProvider as an abstract method, breaking source and binary compatibility for existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations.
issues.textoGolden: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

comentarios.texto: order() was added as an abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes order() on every ServiceLoader-discovered CryptoProvider via Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Any CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface (an external or separately built provider jar on the classpath) will throw AbstractMethodError at detection time, i.e. during AuthzClient.create()/server bootstrap, before any provider is usable. Giving order() a default implementation (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) avoids the binary-incompatibility.

issues.descricao: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order() reversed and silently picks index 0, removing the previous multiple-providers error. WHY: Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so ambiguous classpath (e.g. default+FIPS) now nondeterministically picks one by ServiceLoader order instead of failing fast, risking wrong FIPS vs non-FIPS crypto. HOW: only auto-ignore lower-order providers; throw when the top two have equal order().

Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

detectProvider() no longer fails fast when multiple CryptoProviders are present and instead silently picks the first after sorting by order() descending. All Keycloak providers return the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200), so a tie between two providers is broken by the non-deterministic ServiceLoader iteration order rather than the intended priority. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException forcing the classpath to be corrected; now a deployment with two provider jars (exactly the 'multiple providers on classpath' scenario this PR enables) can silently select the unintended provider — e.g. a non-FIPS/strict provider when FIPS is required — with no error. Use a stable tie-breaker (delegate to the provider name/type) or reject equal top orders instead of relying on ServiceLoader order.

issues.descricao: Claims a wrong-length JOSE signature causes an unchecked exception in concatenatedRSToASN1DER; verifiers catch it and report verification failure, as with the existing providers.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature without validating signature.length==signLength. WHY: short JOSE input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and long input is silently truncated to signLength, breaking the ECDSACryptoProvider contract (IOException on malformed) used by verifier contexts. HOW: check length upfront and throw IOException.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER never validates signature.length == signLength before System.arraycopy(signature,0,r,1,len) / (signature,len,s,1,len). A short JWS signature throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, breaking verification on attacker-controlled input. Validate length and throw IOException.

issues.descricao: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.

comentarios.texto: Single default EC keypair reused for ES256/ES384/ES512: testES384/testES512 names claim larger curves but body signs with the same P-256 key and only pads to larger signLength, so full-width 384/521-bit handling is never exercised. Generate a per-algorithm keypair with the correct curve (e.g. secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) before signing.

Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

issues.descricao: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.

comentarios.texto: Tautological round-trip assertion: rsConcat2 is derived from rsConcat via encode+decode that are inverses if self-consistent, so assertArrayEquals(rsConcat,rsConcat2) passes even if both directions are wrong. Verify against external oracle: Signature.initVerify + verify(asn1Des) and/or compare rsConcat to expected split, not just to itself.

The test only checks self-consistency: it asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(g(asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign))) == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign), i.e. that concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a right inverse of asn1derToConcatenatedRS. It never compares against the original DER `sign`, never verifies the ECDSA signature, and never asserts the emvider output is canonical DER. Because the decoder it reads back with (ASN1Decoder.readLength) accepts non-canonical long-form lengths (e.g. 0x81) and validates only tag numbers, a regression in ASN1Encoder.writeLength that always emitted long form would still round-trip and the test would still pass, even though the produced signature would no longer be valid DER and would be rejected by the Keycloak server / a JDK Signature.verify. Assert the encoded signature is valid DER (e.g. verify it with a JDK Signature, or compare asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign) against a known-good width-padded r||s and assert its length equals algorithm.getSignatureLength()).

The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

issues.descricao: getBouncyCastleProvider in AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns the JDK default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle, contrary to the CryptoProvider contract.
ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags because it only masks the low tag bits, so malformed DER is parsed as valid.

sugestoes.texto: When `host` is nil, for example when the create/update request has no host param, `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Use safe navigation or return early when `host` is blank.

`where(id:).first` returns nil for an unknown id, so `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` raise NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` so that Rails returns a 404 instead.

When `categoryId` is null (for example, a new host saved without picking a category), the server stores `uncategorized_category_id`, but the client sets `category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`. The badge is then empty or wrong until the page reloads. Set the category from the server's returned `category_id` instead of the local `categoryId`.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.
record_for_host queries lower(host) on embeddable_hosts, which has no index on host.
The describe block is named allows_embeddable_host but tests host_allowed?.

sugestoes.texto: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() directly to the result set; for the all-clients resource this is the literal string "Clients", which AvailableRoleMappingResource then passes to realm.getClientById, producing a NullPointerException. Filter out the all-clients resource entry and ensure per-client resources are created with type Clients so findByType matches them.

WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions to throw UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: V1 paths such as the client-removal cleanup listener (AdminPermissions.java:88-91) and the /management/permissions endpoint (ClientResource.java:709-742) still invoke these methods; when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, causing client deletion and the permissions endpoint to fail with an internal error. HOW: implement V2 equivalents for these methods or make the V1 callers guard against V2 before invoking them.

WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...) for every target audience client; when V2 is enabled this returns ClientPermissionsV2 and token exchange fails with an internal error. HOW: provide a V2 implementation of canExchangeTo or route token exchange to the V1 evaluator when V2 is active.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are invoked inside nested forEach without being awaited or collected. WHY: Promise.all at line 497 does not include these promises, so the handler can return success before the cancelled=true updates are persisted; the cron then never cancels the SendGrid batch and the cancelled booking still receives workflow emails. HOW: Collect the returned promises into an array and await them together with the other deletes before sending the cancelled emails.

WHAT: The async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are made inside forEach without being awaited or collected. WHY: The tRPC mutation can finish before reminders are marked cancelled or deleted, allowing rescheduled bookings to keep their old workflow reminders active. HOW: Collect the returned promises and await Promise.all before continuing to the attendee translation block.

WHAT: The workflow router invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach at multiple changed sites (delete workflow, disable event types, delete step, edit step) without awaiting or collecting promises; the edit-step site even uses an async callback. WHY: Cancelling reminders when workflows or steps change can fail silently or return success while reminders remain active. HOW: Replace each forEach with Promise.all(reminders.map(...)) and await the result in each branch.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` but returns `false` from both the `if` branch and the fall-through, so the return value is a constant `false` regardless of the feature flag. Return the computed `enabled` value instead.

The SQL-expression gate is applied only inside `ReadQuery`'s `QueryTypeSQL` case, but `buildCMDNode` reads SQL via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` whenever `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled and the command type is `sql`. Because `FlagExpressionParser` is off by default, the default production path never reaches `ReadQuery` and never hits the gate, so `UnmarshalSQLCommand`->`NewSQLCommand` still builds a live SQLCommand. Apply the SQL expression gate to this nodes.go path as well.

issues.descricao: The variable in TablesList is still named duckDB although it no longer holds a DuckDB instance.

The variable `enabled` in enableSqlExpressions holds the negated flag value, so it is true when SQL expressions are disabled and the name states the opposite of its value.
NewInMemoryDB returns a stateless stub whose methods all return 'not implemented', so its name misleads callers expecting a working in-memory database.

sugestoes.texto: A blocked signup increments `match_count` twice because `UsersController#create` runs `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, each invoking this side-effecting validator. Record signup-attempt statistics once at the signup boundary rather than on every model validation.

Concurrent attempts can load the same `match_count` and both save the same incremented value, losing blocked-attempt statistics. Use an atomic database increment with the timestamp update or lock and reload the row before updating it.

issues.descricao: When the server rejects an email, the signup form marks it with the generic 'invalid email' text instead of the server's reason (blocked or not allowed).

comentarios.texto: The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.
issues.textoGolden: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

comentarios.texto: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of email validation, so each signup attempt (validated twice) inflates the counter and concurrent updates can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

issues.descricao: Claims the 'returns false' spec cannot distinguish nil from false because be_false is a truthiness matcher.

comentarios.texto: This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

issues.descricao: The domain whitelist/blacklist regex @(domains) is not anchored at the end, so an address like user@example.com.evil.com matches a whitelist entry for example.com and bypasses the restriction.
issues.textoGolden: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

issues.descricao: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
A spec comment says last_match_at shows whether an email has ever been blocked, but should_block? updates it on every match, including do_nothing records.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The `GrafanaRuleListItem` rendered inside `rules.map` has no `key` prop, because the old `key={key}` was removed along with GrafanaRuleLoader. WHY: React cannot track list items reliably as pages load and filters change, so it logs key warnings and can reuse or mix up item state, such as the action menu state, across different rules. HOW: pass `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

WHAT: For prom-only Grafana rules, which is the only mode the list view now uses, `rule` is undefined, so the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` condition is always false. `AlertRuleMenu` also gates Delete and Pause on `rulerRule`. WHY: The 'Silence notifications' menu item appears, because the prom ability check passes, but clicking it sets state and no drawer opens. Delete and Pause can never appear in the list view even when the user has permission. HOW: make the silence drawer and delete/pause handlers work from the prom rule. For example, build the drawer input from `promRule` and `groupIdentifier`, or fetch the single ruler rule lazily when the user opens the action.

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

issues.descricao: The comment claims GrafanaPromRuleDTO abilities have no loading state, but the next line makes support depend on the folder loading flag.

comentarios.texto: The comment says there is no loading state, but the next line is `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. `loading` comes from the folder fetch. Update the comment to say that support depends on the folder loading state.

issues.descricao: The Grafana branch of the filtered rule list renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, so React reconciles the streaming list by index and warns about missing keys.
issues.textoGolden: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the filtered list renders <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without a `key` prop, dropping the `key={key}` that the replaced <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../> had. WHY: `rules.map` renders a dynamic list keyed by getRuleKey/hashRule; without a key React logs duplicate-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, so as the async rule stream updates/reorders the wrong rule row can be reused/mutated (stale state, swapped actions). HOW: add `key={key}` (the value is already destructured on line 152) to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element.

WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass key. WHY: Breaks React list reconciliation — wrong item reuse, stale actions/state and console key warnings for every Grafana hit. HOW: Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

issues.descricao: The test named 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks the More button exists, never the menu options.

comentarios.texto: The test 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks that the More button exists. It finds the button by name 'More', so the aria-label and text assertions are tautological. It would pass even if the menu had no actions or the abilities were broken. Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never verifies any action menu option: the body only asserts the More button exists and has aria-label/text 'More'. Either open the menu and assert the menu items, or rename the test to reflect that it only checks the trigger button's rendering/accessibility.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never opens the menu nor asserts menu items — it only checks More button presence/aria/text. Click More and assert expected menuitems (or rename to 'should render More button') so it fails if menu actions break.

issues.descricao: GrafanaGroupLoader's JSDoc still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints after the ruler query was removed.
